principle_1_one_scalar_knob.name: One scalar knob spans the quality/cost frontier
principle_1_one_scalar_knob.summary: A single threshold moves the router continuously between the cheap and the expensive model, so the whole trade-off curve is one parameter sweep rather than a redesign.
principle_1_one_scalar_knob.tradeoff: Trivially tunable and explainable; but the knob controls a traffic SHARE, not an outcome, so it does not transfer across workloads.

principle_2_calibrate_to_a_share.name: Calibrate the threshold to a target expensive-call share
principle_2_calibrate_to_a_share.summary: The threshold is set as a quantile of predicted win rates so that a chosen fraction of calls go to the strong model.
principle_2_calibrate_to_a_share.tradeoff: Gives a predictable budget; gives no quality floor, and the realised share drifts when the traffic distribution changes.

principle_3_measure_the_normalised_gap.name: Score a router by how much of the strong/weak gap it recovers per unit of expensive traffic
principle_3_measure_the_normalised_gap.summary: The headline metric normalises the area under the accuracy-vs-expensive-share curve against the weak and strong endpoints, so routers on different fleets are comparable.
principle_3_measure_the_normalised_gap.tradeoff: Comparable and scale-free; erases absolute dollars and ignores latency entirely.

principle_4_fail_expensive_is_a_choice.name: Decide what an unusable prediction falls back to
principle_4_fail_expensive_is_a_choice.summary: When the predictor emits nothing parseable the win rate is treated as maximal, which routes the request to the expensive model.
principle_4_fail_expensive_is_a_choice.tradeoff: Protects quality on inputs the model cannot score; silently turns predictor breakage into a cost blow-out with no signal.

principle_5_prediction_on_the_hot_path.name: A predictor on the decision path is a dependency on the decision path
principle_5_prediction_on_the_hot_path.summary: Some routers make a blocking remote embedding call for every decision, so the router's own availability and latency now depend on a third service.
principle_5_prediction_on_the_hot_path.tradeoff: Better predictions; a new failure mode and an unbounded added latency per decision.
